title: Fused row-wise softmax (CUDA)
nl_target: Compute row-wise softmax of a (B, N) float32 matrix in a single kernel: subtract per-row max for numerical stability, exp, normalize by per-row sum. Each CUDA block handles one row; intra-block reductions via warp shuffles. For Cerebras: place one row per PE along the Y axis; reduce within a PE.
acceptance_notes: Reference computed via numpy: y = numpy.exp(x - x.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)); y /= y.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True). assert_allclose(rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5). Test both B>1 row distribution and a single-row degenerate case.

title: RMSNorm forward (CUDA)
nl_target: y = (x / sqrt(mean(x*x) + eps)) * gamma per row of a (B, N) matrix; gamma is shape (N,). The compute kernel needs one reduction (sum of squares) and one elementwise pass. On Cerebras, one PE per row along Y; gamma broadcast to every PE.
acceptance_notes: Reference: r = numpy.sqrt((x*x).mean(-1, keepdims=True) + eps); y = (x / r) * gamma. assert_allclose(rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-4).

title: LayerNorm forward (CUDA)
nl_target: y = ((x - mean(x)) / sqrt(var(x) + eps)) * gamma + beta over the last dim of (B, N). Two reductions per row (mean, then var) followed by an elementwise pass; gamma and beta are length N.
acceptance_notes: Reference: mu = x.mean(-1, keepdims=True); sigma = numpy.sqrt(((x-mu)**2).mean(-1, keepdims=True) + eps); y = (x-mu)/sigma * gamma + beta. assert_allclose(rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-4).

title: Flash Attention forward, tiny block (CUDA)
nl_target: Compute attention output O = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(d)) @ V where Q,K,V are (B,H,T,d). Use the online-softmax trick (Flash Attention forward): tile along T_k, maintain running max + running denominator, never materialize the full attention matrix. For Cerebras: a single PE per (B,H) row pair OR a 2D layout that tiles T_q across X and T_k across Y; the same online-softmax recurrence applies per output tile. d small (≤64), T tractable per-PE memory.
acceptance_notes: Reference: numpy implementation. scores = q @ k.T / sqrt(d); attn = softmax(scores, axis=-1); o = attn @ v. assert_allclose(rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3). Test (B=1, H=1, T=128, d=32) at minimum.

title: Sparse @ Dense matrix product (SpMM, CSR sparse, dense RHS)
nl_target: Y = A @ B where A is sparse in CSR form (rowptr, colidx, vals, M-by-K), B is dense (K, N). For each row i of A: Y[i, :] = sum_{nz in row i} vals[nz] * B[colidx[nz], :]. Cerebras layout: row-tiled A across Y axis; each PE processes its assigned rows; B is replicated or row-broadcast as needed.
acceptance_notes: Build A as scipy.sparse.csr_matrix from a random sparsity pattern with fixed density (e.g. 1%); expected = A.toarray() @ B; assert_allclose(rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4).

title: Segmented reduction (sum)
nl_target: Given values[N] and segment_ids[N] (non-decreasing, in [0, G)), produce out[G] = sum of values per segment. Cerebras layout: each PE owns a contiguous chunk of (values, segment_ids); a single boundary fix-up over the row reduces cross-PE segments. For trivial first version: assume the entire input fits in one PE.

title: Batched GEMV: y[b] = A[b] @ x[b]
nl_target: B matrices of shape (M, N) and B vectors (N,) produce B vectors (M,). Cerebras: one batch per PE along Y, GEMV-style row tiling along X; reuse the existing 2D GEMV pattern but with a third batch axis.

title: Inclusive prefix sum (Blelloch up-sweep / down-sweep)
nl_target: Compute y[i] = sum(x[0..=i]). Two-phase tree on a 1D mesh: up-sweep produces per-PE block sums; down-sweep distributes prefix base and finalizes per-PE prefix.

title: 1D direct convolution with a small kernel (K=3, 5, 7)
nl_target: y[i] = sum_k w[k] * x[i + k - K/2]. Halo exchange of K/2 elements at tile boundaries; per-tile @fmacs accumulate.

title: Top-K elements (small K, single PE)
nl_target: Return the K largest values from a length-N float32 vector held entirely on one PE. K small (≤32); use repeated max-and-mask rather than full sort.

title: One Adam optimizer step (fused)
nl_target: Inputs param, grad, m, v (all length N) and scalars lr, beta1, beta2, eps. Compute: m = beta1*m + (1-beta1)*grad; v = beta2*v + (1-beta2)*grad*grad; param -= lr * m / (sqrt(v) + eps). Outputs updated param, m, v. Cerebras: elementwise across a 1D mesh.
acceptance_notes: Compute reference in numpy; assert_allclose for each of param, m, v (rtol=1e-5).

title: Multi-head attention QKV projection
nl_target: Given input X of shape (T, d_model) and a packed weight Wqkv of shape (d_model, 3*d_model), compute Q, K, V each of shape (T, d_model). Three independent matmuls, or one batched matmul, then split the last axis. Cerebras: GEMM-style 2D block layout; split happens host-side after readback.
